title: Blazer Warrior
text: “Heh… Even lowly, evil rogues<mages> like these are more than I alone could ever hope to clean up. That just goes to show how many dark chasers<darkness of men> there are out there. To wipe them out, we need more than a single chaos executioner<enforcer>.”

I couldn't quite follow this bit, I say. From what I could gather, it seemed like Rafumi alone couldn't possibly root out all the troublemakers running amok in Melromarc, and what she wanted were more hands—heroes or otherwise—capable of rounding them up.
“I— I see…”

Even the Queen didn't seem to grasp the phrasing of Rafumi, the body double whose manner of speech Kuro-chan was apparently so fond of. That said, Rafumi turned toward Trash alongside Fleon-chan, threw open her cape with a dramatic swish, spread her arms wide, and declared,

“If you feel that much responsibility, then all the more reason to step onto the battlefield and become a guardian<protector> who protects the people you are meant to protect—quite literally, just as a Shield Hero embodies protection.”
“Guh…”

Apparently Trash still harbored some resistance toward Father, and his face twisted with frustration, so they say. But Rafumi, judging his reaction to be lackluster, turned her attention to the Queen instead.
“Then, Queen, how about you look after your own kingdom in place of the Wise Sage King?”
“Huh?”
“Wha— what are you saying?”

“I'm simply proposing that if his sense of responsibility keeps him from stepping forward, he ought to commit himself fully to a supporting role instead. Surely now you can understand what this queen is thinking?”

Trash turned to look at the Queen and began to mull it over. Apparently figuring out what was going through his mind wasn't hard at all. Rather than Trash—steeped as he was in hatred toward demi-humans and beastmen—the one chosen as the foremost candidate to entrust the kingdom to in his stead had been Éclair's parent. And it was the Queen who had made that selection, leaving her own duties in their hands. In other words, it was the Queen who had correctly grasped Melromarc's future all along. Which meant that if his own failures had brought things to this point, and he couldn't show his face in public because of it, then perhaps if the Queen took up the banner instead… he could finally do something that might let him forgive himself. Or so the thought seemed to cross Trash's face, or so it's said.
“Looks like you've found your answer, hm?”
“If my wife… is willing to do it…”
“There you have it. So, how about it? It all comes down to whether you're willing to act as proxy for the Wise Sage King.”
At that, the Queen's face took on a look of mild trouble, though at the same time it seemed to brim with excited anticipation, I say.
“Very well. It's true that we're short-handed as things stand. I suppose I ought to take a more active role in maintaining public order myself.”
“Ooh! You're really doing it! Fleon will do her best too!”
Well, that was Fleon-chan showing off her enthusiasm. The Queen and Trash exchanged a look, and then she smiled, resolve settling into her chest.
“I suppose I'll do things my own way as well.”
Apparently Trash's sudden burst of motivation was enough to summon his staff into being.

“This is… hm. So you're saying you'll forgive my wavering, indecisive choices? Then I too shall support my wife in earnest, once more. The peace that Lucia sought… I'll pursue it with my wife, our hearts as one!”

And so, having decided that he could forgive himself by taking on a supporting role, Trash gripped his staff and took a determined step forward. Seeing this, the Queen didn't so much grow more motivated as—according to Rafumi—resolve that now was her time to take center stage, or something along those lines, I say.
“I'll lend my strength in all sorts of ways too.”
“Fleon has proposals too!”
Rafumi and Fleon-chan piled right on top of the situation. According to Father, they were the type to pour oil on the fire. Though Fleon-chan wasn't the bad one here, I say!

“Hmm… From what I understand of the heroes' oral traditions, there exists something called Melfilo for those who enforce justice. It seems your daughter is meant to become one, but it would be wise for you two, as her parents, to follow suit. Act as a new Melfilo, a beautiful girl warrior, and play the role of her support.”
“Indeed.”
“This is going to keep us busy. Well then, let's put in a call to the kingdom's technical division. Isoiso.”

And so, with the Queen as the star, an envoy of justice was born, I say. Trash donned a mask and a tailcoat, becoming a warrior who supported the Queen from a distance, while the Queen—fighting in perfect form—became the envoy who captured and judged all those who threatened the kingdom.
“That's way too much! …And why am I even saying that? Who told them to go that far? I mean, wouldn't it be simpler if the Queen just fought normally?”
Father's retort seemed to be referencing something, I say. Apparently it had something to do with that word “isoiso.”
“That wouldn't satisfy Fleon at all.”
“You two really are into transformations and dramatic acting, huh…”
“What are you saying, this late in the game? Isn't that just what an Azott is?”
“Don't lump me in with that! That's a Filolial thing!”
“Well, whether it's Kuro-chan or Fleon-chan, that sort of thing does seem to be their hobby.”
Why is it that Filolials keep producing kids who love this kind of theatrical performance…? Father muttered something along those lines, I say.
“Anyway, so Melty-chan saw the whole thing, and that's why she ran away from home?”
“I don't see why it should matter, do you?”
“I mean, given the family bloodline, isn't she bound to end up cast in the little-queen warrior role eventually? Not as Melfilo, but something like ‘Blazer Mel.’ That's probably why she ran.”

Where did this “blazer warrior” business even leak from? Whose oral tradition from Japan was that? Father muttered. Come to think of it, I do vaguely recall catching a glimpse of a similar warrior on some old TV anime once, I say.

“I guess if we don't unveil a proper Melfilo costume, Blazer Mel might end up erupting into existence for real? No, wait—my own words might be what seals her fate! That is absolutely not allowed. Right, Rafumi-chan?”
“No idea. That's the princess's department to figure out.”
“Her running away is only going to accelerate at this rate… I hear shadows can serve as body doubles too, but maybe Melty-chan will end up heading down that path instead…”
“If that happens, let's name her something like Dark Shadow or Black Shadow.”
“Let's not go in the direction of tormenting Melty-chan, alright?”
In the end, Fiancée fled all the way to a hotel on Cal Mira Island, I say. Apparently she recuperated there together with Filo-tan.
“It's kind of funny how they even manage to catch villains with all that theater, but how are they actually dealing with them afterward?”
“From what I hear, the general procedure is to slap a slave crest on them and put them to work.”
“Huh… I guess they don't actually hold trials, then?”
“They're short-staffed there too, apparently, so the Queen and the others end up doubling as judges.”
“Hm… just how understaffed is Melromarc, exactly?”
“Well, I suppose it's more accurate to say it's us—the heroes—who caused this, isn't it?”
At Rabbit Guy's remark, Father turned his face away.
“Itsuki really did go on a rampage, huh. Though the rest of us took down our fair share too.”
It was mostly Itsuki who'd taken down the kingdom's higher-ups, I say. And no doubt plenty of the judges belonged to the Three Heroes Church faction as well.
“There are plenty of sore losers trying to justify themselves, and others still claiming they were framed or just caught up in it by accident. It's honestly exasperating.”
“Yeah.”
“Hey… you're putting your foot in your mouth, Naofumi.”
Ren furrowed his brow in a troubled way, cautioning Father. Whatever could that have been about, I wonder?
“Fu fu fu… Then shall we go take a look? It'll be amusing. Their faces, that is.”
“No, wait, what exactly are you trying to show us…”

And so Rafumi brought out a vision crystal… showing some section of the castle in Melromarc's castle town, somewhere rarely visited. It appeared to be a building at the front, connected to the prison. Ah, this was that place—the courthouse where judgment was passed on criminals, I say. A line of what looked like bandits or some other sort of criminals was being led along in shackles, hand and foot.
“We shall now pass judgment upon the accused.”
The Queen walked in at an unhurried pace and took her seat at the judge's bench, listening to the charges against the captives.
“The accused are said to have illegally entered our Melromarc and were apprehended while committing acts of plunder in the towns and villages.”
“I see…”
The Queen nodded, looking troubled.
“Well, I suppose in a medieval-style culture, it's normal for royalty to handle judging criminals too.”
“Ah… technically, it's part of a noble's job as well.”
“Sure. By the way, they all pretty much say the same thing in unison, you know? Something like, ‘We're the victims here, attacked by some incomprehensible person called Blazer Millie.’”
Rafumi let out a little snicker.
